title: GPU rendering pipeline via Qt RHI, GLSL JIT, and density-normalized tone mapping
description:
## Problem Statement

Authoring and rendering fractal **Projects** in ChaosKit is currently bottlenecked by CPU-bound **Accumulation** and a legacy OpenGL 3.2 Core display pipeline:

- In the interactive application, **Particles** are stepped one at a time on a single CPU thread via recursive AST interpretation, event-loop timer hops, and mutex-locked **Histogram** writes, while the entire floating-point **Histogram** buffer is repeatedly re-uploaded from CPU memory to the GPU. Previews take minutes or hours to clear noise, making real-time exploration of **Blends**, **Affine Transforms**, **Formulas**, **Coloring Methods**, and **Camera** framing sluggish and grainy.
- Display and headless **Tone Mapping** are hardcoded against OpenGL 3.2 Core contexts and legacy framebuffer items. On macOS (where OpenGL is deprecated and frozen at 4.1 without compute shaders), this prevents GPU compute entirely and blocks native Metal execution, as well as native Vulkan and Direct3D execution on Linux and Windows.
- **Tone Mapping** currently operates on raw, unnormalized **Histogram** hit counts rather than sample density (**Iterations Per Pixel**). Immediately after an edit, low-sample frames appear nearly black and drift brighter over time; under GPU throughput (or deep renders exceeding roughly two hundred hits per pixel at default exposure), pixel values exceed unit brightness and blow out to solid white.
- Interactive **Accumulation** lacks a convergence stopping target (spinning hardware indefinitely after an image has visually converged), UI image export captures through display-scaled scene-graph items rather than pixel-exact **Project** dimensions, and **Particles** with **Infinite Lifetime** that hit mathematical singularities (`NaN` or `Inf`) remain permanently corrupted.

## Solution

Introduce an end-to-end GPU-resident **Rendering** pipeline shared by both the interactive Qt Quick application and the headless `chaoskit-render` CLI, built on Qt 6's cross-platform Rendering Hardware Interface (`QRhi`) so ChaosKit runs natively on Metal (macOS), Vulkan or OpenGL 4.3+ (Linux), and Direct3D 11/12 or Vulkan (Windows), while retaining the CPU engine as a reference implementation, thumbnail evaluator, and automatic fallback.

Authored **Systems** and optional **Cameras** are compiled at runtime from their AST structure into specialized compute shaders cached by structural key, while all continuous numeric parameters (**Affine Transforms**, **Formula** parameters, **Blend** weights, **Formula** weights, **Coloring Method** parameters, and **Lifetime** bounds) are packed into uniform buffers so dragging sliders or handles updates at 60+ FPS with zero shader recompilation. **Particles** step in GPU registers, look up colors in a hardware-filtered **Color Map** LUT texture, and scatter into a lock-free 64-bit fixed-point GPU **Histogram** with zero per-frame CPU-to-GPU transfers. **Tone Mapping** normalizes accumulated **Histogram** values by **Iterations Per Pixel** relative to the `100` IPP baseline, giving constant brightness from the very first progressive frame through arbitrarily deep **Accumulation** without blowing out while remaining backward-compatible with existing **Projects** and golden images.

In the UI, adaptive dispatch pacing maintains ~60 FPS responsiveness, a UI-level target **Iterations Per Pixel** setting (with an `Infinite` toggle) automatically transitions converged renders into an idle `Converged` state distinct from manual user `Pause`, and image export reads back the tone-mapped GPU texture directly at exact **Project** dimensions. In `chaoskit-render`, `--backend auto|gpu|cpu` defaults to GPU acceleration when available and supports bitwise-deterministic `--seed` rendering on both GPU and CPU.

## User Stories

1. As a fractal artist, I want interactive **Accumulation** and **Tone Mapping** to run end-to-end on the GPU without per-frame CPU-to-GPU **Histogram** copies, so that previews converge orders of magnitude faster while I author a **Project**.
2. As a fractal artist on macOS, Linux, or Windows, I want ChaosKit to run natively on my platform's modern GPU API (Metal, Vulkan, Direct3D, or OpenGL 4.3+) without a forced OpenGL 3.2 Core override, so that compute acceleration and zero-copy display work seamlessly across desktop platforms.
3. As a fractal artist, I want dragging **Affine Transform** handles or numeric fields on a **Blend** or **Camera** to update the GPU render via uniform buffers without recompiling shaders, so that spatial manipulation feels instantaneous at 60+ FPS.
4. As a fractal artist, I want dragging **Formula** parameter sliders to update the GPU render without recompiling shaders, so that exploring non-linear shapes is smooth and hitch-free.
5. As a fractal artist, I want dragging **Blend** weight sliders and **Formula** weight sliders to update uniform buffers without recompiling shaders, so that rebalancing a **System** is just as responsive as editing **Formula** parameters.
6. As a fractal artist, I want editing **Coloring Method** parameters and **Lifetime** `[Min, Max]` bounds to update uniform buffers without recompiling shaders, so that tuning color flow and trajectory warm-up never stutters.
7. As a fractal artist, I want structural **System** edits (adding, removing, or toggling **Blends** or **Formulas**, changing **Formula** or **Coloring Method** types, or toggling **Isolated Blend** or **Camera**) to automatically compile a specialized GPU compute pipeline and reset the **Histogram**, so that arbitrary authored **Systems** run at peak native shader speed.
8. As a fractal artist, I want adjusting **Tone Mapping** controls (`gamma`, `exposure`, and `vibrancy`) to immediately re-run **Tone Mapping** over the already-accumulated GPU **Histogram** without clearing it, so that post-processing tweaks are instant and lossless even on deep renders.
9. As a fractal artist, I want switching the active **Color Map** to upload a `1024 × 1` LUT texture and reset **Accumulation** without recompiling the **System** compute shader, so that browsing **Color Maps** is instantaneous and supports any procedural or table-based **Color Map**.
10. As a fractal artist, I want **Tone Mapping** to normalize accumulated **Histogram** sums by current **Iterations Per Pixel** relative to `100` IPP, so that the very first frame after an edit appears at its true final brightness and progressively de-noises rather than starting black and drifting brighter.
11. As a fractal artist, I want deep or `Infinite` renders (`1,000` to `100,000+` **Iterations Per Pixel**) to maintain consistent exposure without clipping to solid white, so that letting a fractal cook longer only improves smoothness and detail.
12. As a fractal artist, I want existing saved `.ck` and text-Protobuf **Projects** (and `100`-IPP CLI renders) to retain their exact expected brightness under `exposure`, `gamma`, and `vibrancy`, so that density-normalized **Tone Mapping** does not break existing artwork or golden reference images.
13. As a fractal artist, I want bright attractor hotspots to accumulate without integer overflow or atomic spin-lock stalls, so that high-contrast attractors render accurately and fast at any resolution and sample depth.
14. As a fractal artist, I want GPU **Formulas** and **Coloring Methods** to match C++ mathematical semantics—including negative bases raised to integer exponents in `pow`, signed fractional parts in `frac`, truncated remainder in `fmod`, signbit-based `signum`, and safe `atan2(0, 0)`—so that every **Formula** looks faithful on GPU and CPU alike.
15. As a fractal artist authoring a **System** with **Infinite Lifetime**, I want any **Particle** whose position or **Color Coordinate** becomes non-finite (`NaN` or `Inf`) due to division by zero or diverging trajectories to be immediately discarded for plotting and revived on the next step (on both GPU and CPU), so that active **Particles** never die permanently over long sessions.
16. As a fractal artist, I want GPU **Accumulation** to honor initial randomized **Lifetime** staggering, deterministic revived `max_lifetime`, and unplotted `min_lifetime` warm-up iterations, so that startup transients and finite-**Lifetime** visual structure match ChaosKit's domain rules.
17. As a fractal artist, I want panning and zooming in the preview viewport to remain an instant, non-destructive 2D loupe over the authored `width × height` **Project** canvas without clearing the **Histogram**, so that I can inspect fine detail freely while using **Camera** as the sole authored framing mechanism.
18. As a fractal artist, I want the UI to adapt per-frame GPU dispatch sizes dynamically toward an ~60 FPS frame budget (starting with a fast lightweight dispatch immediately after edits), so that the desktop and editor controls remain fluid on both integrated laptop GPUs and high-end discrete GPUs.
19. As a fractal artist, I want a UI preview target **Iterations Per Pixel** setting (defaulting to `1000` IPP, plus an `Infinite` toggle) that automatically transitions **Accumulation** into an idle `Converged` state once reached, so that my GPU stops consuming power and spinning fans once the preview is clean.
20. As a fractal artist, I want any visual edit to the **Project** while `Converged` to automatically clear the **Histogram** and resume **Accumulation**, so that I never have to manually unpause after convergence.
21. As a fractal artist, I want raising the target **Iterations Per Pixel** (or toggling `Infinite` on) to clear `Converged` and continue accumulating directly on top of the existing **Histogram** without clearing it, so that I can refine a converged render to higher density without losing work.
22. As a fractal artist, I want manually clicking `Pause` (`running = false`) to stay distinct from `Converged`, so that edits I make while intentionally paused do not unexpectedly start GPU execution until I click `Run`.
23. As a fractal artist, I want the UI preview target **Iterations Per Pixel** and `Infinite` toggle to stay out of the persisted **Project** file schema, so that `.ck` files capture only image appearance and headless CLI batch jobs never hang on `Infinite`.
24. As a fractal artist, I want `Export Image` in the UI to read back the tone-mapped GPU texture directly at the **Project**'s exact `width × height` pixel resolution, so that exported files are never blurred, cropped, or rescaled by screen `devicePixelRatio` or viewport zoom/pan.
25. As a fractal artist, I want **System** lowering warnings (such as normalized **Lifetime** ranges or unrecognized **Formulas**) to continue surfacing via the UI snackbar and CLI `stderr`, so that authoring feedback is preserved.
26. As a CLI user, I want `chaoskit-render` to execute GPU **Accumulation** and **Tone Mapping** completely offscreen without opening a window or creating a swapchain, so that batch scripts and remote servers render at GPU speed cleanly.
27. As a CLI user, I want a `--backend <auto|gpu|cpu>` option on `chaoskit-render` (defaulting to `auto`), so that `chaoskit-render` uses GPU compute automatically when available, falls back cleanly to multi-threaded CPU when hardware compute is unavailable, and lets me force `gpu` or `cpu` explicitly.
28. As a CLI user, I want explicit `--backend gpu` to fail with a clear error message and non-zero exit code when no compute-capable GPU backend is available, so that scripts requesting GPU execution never silently degrade without notice.
29. As a CLI user, I want passing `--seed <uint64>` to produce bitwise-identical output images across repeated runs on the same backend and device for both `--backend gpu` (at full parallel GPU speed via a counter-based PRNG) and `--backend cpu` (single-threaded PCG), so that seeded renders are fast and reproducible.
30. As a CLI user, I want passing `--threads <N>` to control CPU worker concurrency (implicitly selecting CPU when `--backend` is `auto`, and exiting non-zero with a clear error if combined with explicit `--backend gpu`), so that existing `--threads` invocations stay backward-compatible and unambiguous.
31. As a library consumer and maintainer, I want `ast`, `core`, and `library` to remain Qt-free and licensed under `Apache 2.0` (including the pure C++ AST-to-GLSL compiler and uniform packer), while `QRhi` and `QShaderBaker` dependencies stay confined to `GPLv3` Qt targets, so that licensing and dependency boundaries remain clean.
32. As a developer, I want small `Formula` gallery previews to continue evaluating on the CPU `SystemProcessor`, so that generating tiny grid thumbnails avoids unnecessary GPU shader-compilation overhead.
33. As a developer, I want CI to run sandbox-safe compiler/CPU unit tests in `make test-unit` and full end-to-end `QRhi` compute parity tests across Metal (macOS CI) and software Vulkan `lavapipe` (Linux CI) in `make test`, so that regressions in shader generation, math parity, or **Tone Mapping** are caught automatically on every pull request.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Module & Licensing Architecture (ADR-0005)**:
  - Keep `ast`, `core`, and `library` completely free of Qt and external GPU SDKs under `Apache 2.0`. Place the pure C++ AST-to-GLSL compute shader generator, structural key builder, and uniform packer in this Qt-free layer.
  - Place the Qt 6 `QRhi` execution engine, runtime `QShaderBaker` shader-baking wrapper (`Qt6::GuiPrivate` and `Qt6::ShaderToolsPrivate`), GPU resource management, and `QRhi` **Tone Mapping** pass in the `GPLv3` Qt layer shared by both the interactive UI application and `chaoskit-render`.
  - Retain the CPU `CameraSystemProcessor` and multi-threaded CPU **Accumulation** path for unit tests, `Formula` preview thumbnails, GPU-less fallback, and `--backend cpu`.
  - Make **zero changes** to the Protocol Buffer `Project` schema.

- **Cross-Platform `QRhi` & `QQuickRhiItem` Integration (Superseding OpenGL 3.2 Core in ADR-0004)**:
  - Remove the forced OpenGL 3.2 Core surface format override in the UI application so Qt Quick automatically selects the platform's native RHI backend (Metal on macOS, Vulkan or OpenGL 4.3+ on Linux, Direct3D 11/12 or Vulkan on Windows).
  - Migrate `SystemView` from `QQuickFramebufferObject` to `QQuickRhiItem` (`QQuickRhiItemRenderer`), configuring fixed color-buffer dimensions matching `Project` `width` and `height` so compute **Accumulation** dispatches and the **Tone Mapping** graphics pass record directly onto Qt Quick's command buffer with zero cross-API copies.
  - If the active UI `QRhi` device lacks `QRhi::Compute` support at runtime, fall back gracefully to multi-threaded CPU **Accumulation** feeding the same `QRhi` **Tone Mapping** pass inside `SystemView`.
  - In `chaoskit-render`, initialize a swapchain-free offscreen `QRhi` instance (probing platform native backends in priority order: Metal on macOS; Vulkan then OpenGL on Linux; Direct3D 11/12 then Vulkan on Windows) and execute frames via `beginOffscreenFrame` + texture readback. Both GPU **Accumulation** and CPU **Accumulation** route through the shared `QRhi` **Tone Mapping** pass so legacy `GLToneMapper` and raw OpenGL contexts are retired completely.

- **Runtime JIT Shader Compilation & Structural Pipeline Cache**:
  - Lower `CameraSystem` (**System** AST + optional **Camera** AST) into a Vulkan-flavored GLSL (`#version 450`) compute shader string and bake it in-memory via `QShaderBaker` into SPIR-V plus native translated shader variants (MSL, HLSL, GLSL) packaged as a `QShader`.
  - Compute a deterministic structural key over `CameraSystem` that captures AST topology, transform variants, **Formula** expression trees, **Coloring Method** expression trees, and **Camera** presence while **ignoring** all `TransformParams` float values, `RandomChoiceTransform` **Blend** weights, `WeightedSumTransform` **Formula** weights, and **Lifetime** bounds.
  - Cache compiled `QShader` / `QRhiComputePipeline` objects by structural key so slider and transform drags never invoke `QShaderBaker` or recreate GPU pipelines.

- **Uniform Buffer Packing**:
  - Pack all continuous parameters into a `std140`-compatible uniform buffer (`vec4`-packed float array + scalar metadata):
    - Flattened `TransformParams` values (**Affine Transform** coefficients, **Formula** parameters, **Coloring Method** parameters) in deterministic AST traversal order,
    - Normalized cumulative probability thresholds for `RandomChoiceTransform` (**Blend** weights, guarding zero-total-weight systems as no-op transforms),
    - Scalar weights for `WeightedSumTransform` (**Formula** weights),
    - Normalized **Lifetime** `[Min, Max]` (including `Infinite`), revival bounds `[-1, 1]^2`, aspect-ratio-preserving zoom-to-fill coordinate-to-pixel transform, canvas `(width, height)`, ticks per invocation `K`, seed values, and dispatch step offset.

- **Workgroup Iteration, Math Parity, & Non-Finite Particle Revival**:
  - Use **Pure Compute Scatter** with **Per-Thread In-Register** execution: maintain a persistent GPU storage buffer of **Particles** (`x`, `y`, `colorCoordinate`, `lifetime`, `warmup`, and PRNG state when unseeded). Each GPU invocation loads its **Particle** into registers, runs `K` single-step ticks, and stores the updated **Particle** back once per dispatch.
  - Initialize the **Particle** pool with staggered initial **Lifetimes** in `[min(min_lifetime + 1, max_lifetime), max_lifetime]` (or `Infinite`) and `warmup = min_lifetime` per ADR-0003. On each tick: if `lifetime == 0`, revive position in `[-1, 1]^2` and **Color Coordinate** in `[0, 1]` with `lifetime = max_lifetime` and `warmup = min_lifetime`; step the **System** once (decrementing finite `lifetime`); if the resulting `x`, `y`, or `colorCoordinate` is non-finite (`isnan` or `isinf`), set `lifetime = 0` and `warmup = 0` without plotting; else if `warmup > 0`, decrement `warmup` without plotting; else evaluate the optional **Camera** on a copy of the **Particle**, sample the **Color Map** LUT, scatter to the **Histogram** if within `[0, width) × [0, height)`, and count one plotted iteration (via workgroup-reduced atomic addition into a 64-bit plotted-iteration counter so `currentIpp` accurately reflects true plotted iterations regardless of warm-up or singularities).
  - Apply the identical non-finite (`NaN`/`Inf`) **Particle** revival rule in CPU `SystemProcessor` so CPU and GPU share identical domain behavior under singularities and **Infinite Lifetime**.
  - Emit C++-faithful GLSL math helpers matching `ExpressionInterpreter`:
    - `POWER`: support negative bases when the exponent is an integer value (computing `abs(base)^exp` and negating when the integer exponent is odd) and guard `0^0` / negative non-integer bases cleanly instead of emitting raw undefined GLSL `pow`.
    - `FRAC`: `x - trunc(x)` (matching `std::modf`).
    - `MODULO`: `a - b * trunc(a / b)` with zero-divisor guard (matching `std::fmod`).
    - `SIGNUM`: `-1.0` when negative/signbit set, `+1.0` otherwise.
    - `ATAN2`: return `0.0` when both arguments are `0.0`, otherwise two-argument `atan(first, second)`.

- **Color Map LUT & Lock-Free 64-Bit Fixed-Point Histogram**:
  - Represent the active **Color Map** on the GPU as a `1024 × 1` `RGBA32F` 2D `QRhiTexture` sampled from `core::ColorMap` with linear filtering and `ClampToEdge` addressing. Changing the **Color Map** updates only this texture and clears the **Histogram**.
  - Represent the GPU **Histogram** as a storage buffer of `width * height * 8` `uint32` words (`32` bytes/pixel): four channels `(R, G, B, Count)`, each stored as a lock-free 64-bit carry-pair `(lo, hi)` of `uint32` values in fixed-point (e.g., `Q40.24` scale `2^24`, updating via `uint old = atomicAdd(lo, v); if (old + v < old) atomicAdd(hi, 1u);`). This uses only universally supported 32-bit `uint` `atomicAdd`, avoids CAS spin-loops on hotspots, prevents overflow across billions of hits per pixel, and is commutative and associative (order-independent).

- **Density-Normalized Tone Mapping**:
  - Reconstruct floating-point `(sumR, sumG, sumB, count)` per pixel in the `QRhi` **Tone Mapping** fragment shader (from the 64-bit fixed-point GPU **Histogram** SSBO on the GPU path, or from the uploaded `RGBA32F` **Histogram** on the CPU path).
  - When `count <= 0` or `currentIpp <= 0`, output opaque black `(0, 0, 0, 1)`. Otherwise multiply `(sumR, sumG, sumB, count)` by `float(100.0 / currentIpp)`—where `currentIpp = double(totalPlottedIterations) / double(width * height)`—before applying the logarithmic exposure, gamma, and vibrancy curve. At `100` **Iterations Per Pixel**, the scale factor is `1.0`, preserving exact backward compatibility with existing `exposure` values and golden images.

- **Interactive Pacing, Convergence Lifecycle, & Pixel-Exact Export**:
  - Expose `targetIterationsPerPixel` (default `1000`), `infiniteAccumulation` (default `false`), read-only `currentIterationsPerPixel`, and read-only `converged` on `SystemView` alongside UI controls in the image/preview settings.
  - Maintain distinct `running` (user manual Run/Pause) and `converged` states:
    - When `running == true` and `!converged`, schedule frames continuously and adapt dispatch size (`workgroups × K`) using exponential smoothing of frame/compute duration to target ~8–12 ms per frame (~60 FPS), resetting to a small initial bootstrap dispatch right after any **Histogram** clear for immediate visual feedback while dragging.
    - When `!infiniteAccumulation && currentIterationsPerPixel >= targetIterationsPerPixel`, set `converged = true` and stop further compute dispatches after presenting the tone-mapped result.
    - Any visual edit to **System**, **Color Map**, or **Project** `width`/`height` clears the **Histogram**, resets `currentIterationsPerPixel = 0` and `converged = false`, and immediately dispatches if `running == true` (while staying paused if `running == false`).
    - Increasing `targetIterationsPerPixel` above `currentIterationsPerPixel` or toggling `infiniteAccumulation = true` sets `converged = false` and resumes **Accumulation** on top of the existing **Histogram** without clearing.
  - Implement an asynchronous/callback-based export method on `SystemView` that schedules a `QRhi` texture readback of the tone-mapped `width × height` color target and writes it via `QImageWriter`, replacing scene-graph `grabToImage` in the UI export flow.

- **CLI Flags & Deterministic Seeded GPU Execution**:
  - Add `--backend <auto|gpu|cpu>` (default `auto`) to `chaoskit-render`.
  - If `--threads <N>` is explicitly provided: when `--backend` is `gpu`, exit non-zero with a descriptive error; when `--backend` is `auto` or `cpu`, run the CPU backend with `N` threads (preserving existing `--threads` CLI behavior and `--seed` + `--threads > 1` validation on CPU).
  - When `--seed <uint64>` is supplied on the GPU backend, generate all random numbers in the compute shader via a stateless counter-based PRNG (such as Philox-4x32 or PCG-hash keyed by `(seed, particleId, globalTickIndex, drawSubIndex)`) using fixed deterministic dispatch chunking so two invocations with the same `--seed` on the same GPU produce bit-for-bit identical output images (`bytes1 == bytes2`) at full parallel GPU speed.

## Testing Decisions

- **What Makes a Good Test**:
  - Tests must assert observable external behavior at the highest possible boundaries rather than internal implementation details (no assertions on generated GLSL source text, internal uniform buffer indices, or private helper classes).
  - Stochastic GPU-vs-CPU equivalence is verified statistically via normalized Root Mean Square Error (`RMSE <= 0.05`) on converged renders, while seeded determinism (`--seed`) is verified via byte-for-byte output equality across repeated runs on the same backend and device.

- **Modules & Seams Under Test**:
  1. **Existing CLI End-to-End Seam (`cli` test target, CTest `gpu` label)**:
     - Invokes `chaoskit-render` as an external process (`(CLI args, Project file) -> (exit code, stderr, output image)`).
     - Verifies `--backend auto|gpu|cpu` selection, explicit `--backend gpu` vs `--backend cpu` visual parity (`RMSE <= 0.05`) across fixtures covering library **Formulas** (including negative-base integer `pow` in `Ex` and zero-division singularities in `Spherical`/`Hyperbolic`), **Affine Transforms**, **Coloring Methods**, **Color Maps**, **Camera**, **Isolated Blend**, and finite/infinite **Lifetime** warm-up.
     - Verifies same-backend `--seed` bitwise determinism (`bytes1 == bytes2`) on `--backend gpu` as well as `--backend cpu`.
     - Verifies density-normalized **Tone Mapping** (`currentIpp / 100.0`): confirms backward compatibility with the checked-in `100`-IPP golden image, and verifies that rendering the same **Project** at low (`5` IPP), baseline (`100` IPP), and high (`2,000` IPP) densities preserves consistent overall image luminance without blacking out or blowing out to white.
     - Verifies CLI error handling for invalid `--backend` values and `--backend gpu` combined with `--threads`.
  2. **New Interactive UI Component Seam (`ui` test target, CTest `gpu` label)**:
     - Hosts `SystemView` (`QQuickRhiItem`) in a `QQuickWindow` bound to `ProjectModel` and drives it strictly through `ProjectModel` mutations and `SystemView`'s QML-facing properties, signals, and export slot.
     - Verifies that mutating continuous parameters (**Affine Transforms**, **Formula** params, **Blend** weights, **Formula** weights, **Coloring Method** params, **Lifetime**) resets **Accumulation** and updates output *without* incrementing compiled-shader pipeline count, whereas structural **System** mutations (`addBlend`, `deleteBlendAt`, `addFormula`, changing **Formula** or **Coloring Method** type, toggling **Camera** or **Isolated Blend**) recompile cleanly; verifies that `gamma`/`exposure`/`vibrancy` edits update the rendered output *without* resetting `currentIterationsPerPixel`.
     - Verifies the `Converged` vs. manual `Paused` (`running`) state machine: hitting `targetIterationsPerPixel` sets `converged == true` and halts accumulation; visual edits clear `converged` and resume when `running == true` while never overriding `running == false`; raising `targetIterationsPerPixel` or enabling `infiniteAccumulation` resumes accumulating without resetting `currentIterationsPerPixel`.
     - Verifies that direct `SystemView` image export produces an image with exact `Project` `(width, height)` dimensions regardless of QML `zoom`, translation, or `Screen.devicePixelRatio`.
  3. **Existing Sandbox-Safe Unit Seam (`core` and compiler unit test targets, excluded from `gpu` label so `make test-unit` runs everywhere)**:
     - Extends `SystemProcessor` unit tests to verify that non-finite (`NaN`/`Inf`) **Particles** are immediately marked expired without plotting and revived on the next step under both finite and **Infinite Lifetime**.
     - Tests the `CameraSystem`-to-`QShader` compiler + `QShaderBaker` boundary purely in CPU memory (no GPU or display required): verifies that every `FormulaType` in `library` and every `ColoringMethodType` bakes into a valid `QShader` with zero errors, and that parameter/weight/**Lifetime** mutations leave the structural key unchanged while structural AST mutations produce distinct keys.

- **CI Environment & Prior Art**:
  - Install Mesa's software Vulkan 1.3 driver (`lavapipe` / `mesa-vulkan-drivers` and `libvulkan1`) on Linux CI runners so `make test` executes the full `QRhi` Vulkan compute + `QShaderBaker` pipeline on Linux alongside native Metal compute on macOS Apple Silicon runners.
  - Follow the existing GTest + CMake `LABELS "gpu"` registration pattern established by `cli` and `core`/`ui` test suites.

## Out of Scope

- Cuburn-style workgroup-uniform **Blend** selection with `shared`-memory **Particle** pool permutation (kept as a potential future Phase-2 JIT codegen optimization for high-**Blend**-count **Systems** if profiling warrants it).
- Persisting interactive preview `targetIterationsPerPixel` or `infiniteAccumulation` settings in the `Project` Protocol Buffer schema.
- Viewport-coupled re-accumulation on UI pan/zoom (UI pan/zoom remains a non-destructive 2D canvas loupe; **Camera** remains the sole framing mechanism).
- Multi-pixel spatial filter splatting or variable-width density-estimation post-processing filters.
- Bit-for-bit identical pixel output *across* different backends or GPU vendors (cross-backend equivalence is statistical via normalized RMSE; bitwise `--seed` determinism applies to repeated runs on the same backend and device).

## Further Notes

- Core architectural trade-offs—including Qt 6 `QRhi` + `QQuickRhiItem` under `GPLv3`, runtime GLSL JIT compilation via `QShaderBaker`, pure compute in-register **Accumulation** (avoiding Apple Silicon TBDR point-binning bottlenecks), lock-free 64-bit carry-pair fixed-point atomics, and `currentIpp / 100.0` density-normalized **Tone Mapping**—are recorded in ADR-0005, which partially supersedes the OpenGL 3.2 Core specifics of ADR-0004 while building on externalized parameters (ADR-0002) and **Particle** **Lifetime** rules (ADR-0003).
- Before or during implementation, check open backlog issue `chaoskit-9gb` (CPU particle-to-histogram consolidation), as retiring `HistogramGenerator`/`BlenderTask`/`GLToneMapper` in favor of the shared `QRhi` pipeline and CPU fallback largely supersedes or reshapes that task.

title: Prefactor Qt-free CPU Accumulation with non-finite Particle revival and plotted-iteration tracking
description:
## Parent

chaoskit-196

## What to build

Ensure CPU **Particle** stepping immediately discards any **Particle** whose position or **Color Coordinate** becomes non-finite (`NaN` or `Inf`) without plotting and revives it on the next step under both finite and **Infinite Lifetime**. Consolidate CPU **Accumulation** into a single Qt-free batch engine (`Apache 2.0`) shared by `chaoskit-render` and interactive preview rendering—unifying aspect-ratio-preserving zoom-to-fill canvas framing, `min_lifetime` warm-up, **Color Map** lookup, single-threaded seeded execution, multi-threaded batch execution, atomic **System** / **Color Map** / canvas-size resets without stale hits, and exact plotted-iteration counting—while retiring the legacy per-**Particle** event-loop timer worker chain and unused legacy CPU generator classes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Any **Particle** whose stepped `x`, `y`, or **Color Coordinate** is `NaN` or `Inf` is marked expired without plotting and revived cleanly on the next step under both finite and **Infinite Lifetime**
- [ ] A single Qt-free CPU **Accumulation** engine (`Apache 2.0`) executes **Particle** batches with aspect-ratio-preserving zoom-to-fill coordinate mapping, **Lifetime** staggering and `min_lifetime` warm-up, **Camera** evaluation, and **Color Map** lookup
- [ ] Exact total plotted iterations (excluding warm-up and discarded non-finite steps) are tracked alongside the **Histogram**
- [ ] Both `chaoskit-render` (single-threaded seeded and multi-threaded unseeded) and interactive preview rendering use the shared Qt-free CPU **Accumulation** engine, and legacy per-**Particle** timer workers and unused generator classes are removed

title: Consolidate System lowering into a single pass with a core Lifetime value type
description:
## Problem Statement

Lowering an authored **System** from its Protocol Buffer representation into an executable `CameraSystem` (AST structure plus externalized `TransformParams` keyed by `TransformIndex`) currently splits the **Blend** layout rules across multiple independent traversals:

1. One traversal builds the `ast::Transform` tree (`pre` **Affine Transform**, `WeightedSumTransform` of **Formulas**, `post` **Affine Transform**, and **Coloring Method** expression, plus enabled-**Blend** filtering and **Isolated Blend** selection).
2. A second traversal re-derives the exact same conditional branches to walk `TransformIndex` (`firstChild`, `nextSibling`, `parent`) and populate `TransformParams`.
3. The **Formula** preview generator constructs a third, hand-indexed `MultiStepTransform` with literal `TransformIndex{0}` and `TransformIndex{1}` paths.
4. **Particle** **Lifetime** rules (`[Min, Max]` or `Infinite`) are split across the QML editor, `SystemModel`, `SystemView`, and `SystemProcessor`, and **Lifetime** is passed to the generator over a separate side channel (`setLifetimeRange`) after `setSystem`. Because `SystemModel::setMinLifetime` compares `min > max_lifetime` directly, editing `minLifetime` while `isInfiniteLifetime` is active (`max_lifetime == -1`) is broken and rejects every non-negative value.
5. Unchecked inputs in loaded or hand-edited **Project** files—such as an unrecognized **Formula** type string or an out-of-range **Isolated Blend** index—throw or read out of bounds on the GUI thread during lowering, and invalid **Lifetime** values only log a console warning without normalizing the state or informing the user in the UI.

## Solution

Consolidate **System** and **Blend** lowering into a single-pass lowering module and introduce a dedicated `Lifetime` value type carried directly inside `CameraSystem`:

- A single-pass lowering builder walks each **Blend** and **System** once, emitting AST nodes and claiming their corresponding `TransformIndex` parameter slots simultaneously so structure and parameter indices cannot drift apart.
- Expose single-**Blend** lowering (`toTransformSystem`) alongside full **System** lowering (`toCameraSystem`) so the **Formula** preview provider reuses the same lowering module instead of hardcoding `TransformIndex` paths.
- Introduce a `Lifetime` value type in `core` that enforces the `[Min, Max]` / `Infinite` invariant, normalizes out-of-range values when needed, and encapsulates initial random **Lifetime** assignment vs. deterministic revived **Lifetime** assignment (per ADR-0003).
- Embed `Lifetime` inside `CameraSystem` so `CameraSystemProcessor` applies it automatically and the separate `setLifetimeRange` channel across `Generator`, `HistogramGenerator`, and `BlenderTask` is removed.
- Make lowering resilient: sanitize invalid `Lifetime` bounds, skip unrecognized **Formula** types (omitting `WeightedSumTransform` if no valid **Formulas** remain), and fall back to enabled **Blends** when an **Isolated Blend** index is out of range, while recording human-readable warning messages that are logged and surfaced to the user via the main window's `Snackbar`.
- Update `SystemModel` to enforce the same `Lifetime` rules in the UI, fixing the bug where `minLifetime` cannot be edited when **Lifetime** is `Infinite`.

## User Stories

1. As a fractal author, I want to edit the minimum **Particle** **Lifetime** while **Lifetime** is set to `Infinite`, so that I can control the number of unplotted warm-up iterations even when **Particles** never expire.
2. As a fractal author, I want the UI to reject negative `minLifetime` values and `maxLifetime` values below `1` (unless `Infinite`), so that I cannot accidentally configure an invalid **Lifetime** range from the editor.
3. As a fractal author, I want `minLifetime` to automatically clamp down to `maxLifetime` when I switch from `Infinite` (or a larger maximum) to a finite `maxLifetime` smaller than the current `minLifetime`, so that the `[Min, Max]` invariant is always preserved.
4. As a fractal author opening a `.ck` **Project** file that contains an unrecognized **Formula** type, I want ChaosKit to skip that **Formula**, continue rendering the rest of the **Blend**, and show a warning in the `Snackbar`, so that the application does not crash on the GUI thread.
5. As a fractal author opening a `.ck` **Project** file where every **Formula** in a **Blend** has an unrecognized type, I want the **Blend** to lower cleanly with only its `pre` and `post` **Affine Transforms** and **Coloring Method** intact, so that the remaining steps still receive their expected parameter slots.
6. As a fractal author opening a `.ck` **Project** file with an out-of-range **Isolated Blend** index, I want ChaosKit to fall back to rendering all enabled **Blends** and show a warning in the `Snackbar`, so that an invalid isolation index does not cause an out-of-bounds read.
7. As a fractal author opening a `.ck` **Project** file with invalid **Lifetime** numbers (such as negative `min_lifetime`, non-positive finite `max_lifetime`, or `min_lifetime > max_lifetime`), I want ChaosKit to clamp the **Lifetime** into a valid range and show a warning in the `Snackbar`, so that the **System** still renders safely.
8. As a fractal author viewing **Formula** previews in the picker, I want the preview renderer to lower its example `pre` **Affine Transform** and **Formula** through the standard **Blend** lowering module, so that previews always match the parameter-slot layout used by the main renderer.
9. As a fractal author adjusting **Lifetime** settings, I want newly created **Particles** to receive a randomized initial **Lifetime** while revived **Particles** receive the full `maxLifetime` (per ADR-0003), so that startup transients are smoothed while **Lifetime** adjustments remain visually predictable.
10. As a developer maintaining ChaosKit, I want AST structure construction and `TransformIndex` parameter slot assignment for a **Blend** to happen in a single pass, so that changing how a **Blend** lowers only requires editing one traversal.
11. As a developer maintaining ChaosKit, I want `CameraSystem` to carry its `Lifetime` value directly, so that updating a **System** on a processor or generator updates its **Transform**, **Camera**, and **Lifetime** atomically through one interface.

## Implementation Decisions

- **`core::Lifetime` value type**:
  - Represents a **Particle** **Lifetime** range `[min, max]` where `max` is either a positive integer (`>= 1`) or `INFINITE_LIFETIME` (`-1`), and `min >= 0` with `min <= max` whenever `max` is finite.
  - Default value is `min = 0`, `max = INFINITE_LIFETIME`.
  - Provides a normalizing factory/constructor that clamps `min = std::max(0, min)`, treats `max == INFINITE_LIFETIME` as infinite while clamping any other `max < 1` to `1`, and clamps `min = std::min(min, max)` when finite, reporting whether normalization occurred so callers can emit a warning.
  - Provides helper methods for **Particle** lifecycle management following ADR-0003:
    - Initial **Particle** **Lifetime** draw: returns `INFINITE_LIFETIME` when infinite, otherwise `rng.randomInt(std::min(min + 1, max), max)`.
    - Revived **Particle** **Lifetime**: returns `max` (which is `INFINITE_LIFETIME` when infinite).
    - Warm-up count: returns `min`.
  - Supports equality comparison (`==`, `!=`) and debug stream output (`operator<<`).
- **Embedding `Lifetime` in `core::CameraSystem`**:
  - Add `Lifetime lifetime` as a field on `core::CameraSystem` (included in `operator==` / `operator!=` and debug printing).
  - `CameraSystemProcessor` initializes its `SystemProcessor` `Lifetime` from `CameraSystem::lifetime` in its constructor and updates it inside `setCameraSystem(const CameraSystem&)`.
  - `SystemProcessor` stores a `Lifetime` member instead of separate raw `min_lifetime_` / `max_lifetime_` integers (retaining convenience setters/getters on `SystemProcessor` where useful for direct unit tests).
  - Remove `setLifetimeRange(int32_t, int32_t)` from `core::Generator`, `ui::HistogramGenerator`, and `ui::BlenderTask`, and remove the separate `generator_->setLifetimeRange(...)` call from `SystemView::updateSystem()`.
- **Single-pass lowering in `ui/storage/conversions`**:
  - Replace the separate `toTransform` and `populateParams` / `toParams` traversals with a single-pass builder that tracks the current `core::TransformIndex` while constructing `ast::Transform` nodes and writing parameter vectors into `core::TransformParams` at the same time.
  - Expose two functions in `ui/storage/conversions`:
    - `core::TransformSystem toTransformSystem(const Blend& blendProto, std::vector<std::string>* warnings = nullptr)`
    - `core::CameraSystem toCameraSystem(const System& systemProto, std::vector<std::string>* warnings = nullptr)`
  - When lowering a **Blend**:
    - If `has_pre()`, emit `ast::AffineTransform` and claim the current child `TransformIndex` for its 6 matrix parameters.
    - For `formulas()`, resolve each `Formula::type()` via `magic_enum::enum_cast<library::FormulaType>`. If a type is unrecognized (or `FormulaType::Invalid`), append a warning message (if `warnings != nullptr`) and skip it. Only if at least one valid **Formula** remains, emit `ast::WeightedSumTransform` at the next step `TransformIndex` and assign each valid **Formula**'s parameters to its corresponding child `TransformIndex`.
    - If `has_post()`, emit `ast::AffineTransform` and claim the next sibling `TransformIndex` for its 6 matrix parameters.
    - If `has_coloring_method()`, attach the corresponding coloring expression to the `MultiStepTransform` and store its scalar parameter at the **Blend**'s parent `TransformIndex`.
  - When lowering a **System**:
    - Normalize `(min_lifetime, max_lifetime)` into `core::Lifetime`; if normalization adjusted either bound, record a warning message.
    - If `has_isolated_blend()`, check whether `isolated_blend().index()` is within `[0, blends_size())`. If valid, lower only that **Blend** at the root `TransformIndex`. If out of bounds, record a warning message and fall back to lowering all enabled **Blends** inside a `RandomChoiceTransform`.
    - If `has_camera()` and `camera().enabled()`, lower `camera()` via `toTransformSystem(systemProto.camera(), warnings)`.
- **Reuse in `FormulaPreviewProvider`**:
  - In `FormulaPreviewProvider`, build a temporary `Blend` proto with the example `pre` **Affine Transform** and single **Formula** with weight `1.0` and example parameters, and lower it through `toTransformSystem` rather than manually constructing `TransformIndex{0}` and `TransformIndex{1}`.
- **`SystemModel` validation and UI warning surfacing**:
  - In `SystemModel::setMinLifetime(int min)`: reject `min < 0`; if `!isInfiniteLifetime()`, reject `min > maxLifetime()`; allow any `min >= 0` when `isInfiniteLifetime()` is true.
  - In `SystemModel::setMaxLifetime(int max)`: reject `max < 1` unless `max == core::SystemParticle::INFINITE_LIFETIME`; when `max` is finite and `minLifetime() > max`, clamp `min_lifetime` down to `max` and emit `minLifetimeChanged()`.
  - When `SystemView::updateSystem()` lowers the **System** proto via `toCameraSystem(systemProto, &warnings)`, log any warning messages with `qCWarning` and surface them to the user via a signal wired to `openSnackbar(...)` in `MainWindow.qml`.

## Testing Decisions

- **What makes a good test**:
  - Tests should exercise modules through their public interfaces (`toCameraSystem`, `toTransformSystem`, `SystemProcessor`, `CameraSystemProcessor`, and `SystemModel`) and assert observable outputs (`CameraSystem` values, `Particle` states after stepping with a deterministic `Rng`, emitted signals, and collected warning strings), not internal helper functions.
- **Modules to be tested**:
  - `ui/storage/conversions`:
    - Existing tests in `conversions_test` updated to verify that `CameraSystem` includes the expected `Lifetime`.
    - New tests in `conversions_test` for `toTransformSystem(const Blend&)`.
    - New tests for fallback and warning collection: unknown **Formula** type alongside a valid **Formula**, a **Blend** where all **Formulas** are unknown (verifying `post` still lands at the right `TransformIndex`), out-of-range `isolated_blend` index falling back to enabled **Blends**, and invalid `min_lifetime` / `max_lifetime` clamping with warnings.
    - Behavioral round-trip test: lower a `System` with `pre`, **Formula**, `post`, **Coloring Method**, and **Camera**, run a **Particle** through `CameraSystemProcessor`, and assert the resulting **Particle** coordinates and **Color Coordinate** (verifying that lowered `TransformIndex` slots match `TransformInterpreter`).
  - `core::Lifetime`, `core::SystemProcessor`, and `core::CameraSystemProcessor`:
    - Unit tests for `Lifetime` normalization and invariants.
    - Existing `SystemProcessorTest` suite (preserving `CreatesParticleWithRandomLifetime*` and `RevivesDeadParticle*` per ADR-0003).
    - Test in `CameraSystemProcessorTest` verifying that `CameraSystem::lifetime` is applied when constructing or updating `CameraSystemProcessor`.
  - `ui::SystemModel`:
    - Unit test verifying `setMinLifetime` succeeds when `isInfiniteLifetime` is true, rejects negative values, rejects `min > max` when finite, and clamps `minLifetime` when `setMaxLifetime` lowers a finite `max` below `min`.
- **Prior art**:
  - `ui/storage/conversions_test.cpp`, `core/SystemProcessorTest.cpp`, and `core/CameraSystemProcessorTest.cpp` (GoogleTest / GoogleMock).

## Out of Scope

- Refactoring `HistogramGenerator`, `BlenderTask`, `GathererTask`, and `SimpleHistogramGenerator` into a Qt-free render session (tracked in `chaoskit-9gb`).
- Automatic child registration and change-kind propagation in `BaseModel` (tracked in `chaoskit-fth`).
- Managing `isolated_blend` index updates on **Blend** deletion in `SystemModel` and centralizing authoring defaults (tracked in `chaoskit-fu9`).
- Changing the initial random **Lifetime** vs. deterministic revived **Lifetime** behavior (recorded in ADR-0003).

title: Headless CLI renderer (chaoskit-render) and end-to-end golden image tests
description:
## Problem Statement

During development of ChaosKit, rendering a **Project** requires launching the interactive Qt Quick application, manually loading or configuring a **System**, waiting for **Particles** to accumulate into the **Histogram** over an unspecified wall-clock interval, and manually exporting the image. Because there is no headless command-line entry point that shares the Qt implementation's **Project** lowering, coordinate-to-pixel gathering, **Color Map** lookup, and OpenGL **Tone Mapping** pipeline, developers cannot quickly render **Projects** from the command line or write automated end-to-end tests that verify visual rendering output against known reference images (modulo stochastic simulation variance).

## Solution

Provide a standalone headless CLI executable (`chaoskit-render`) in a top-level CLI module that loads a serialized **Project** (in either binary Protobuf or human-readable Protobuf text format), optionally overrides **Project** rendering parameters via command-line flags, executes **Particle** simulation and **Histogram** accumulation using the shared Qt/core rendering components, runs the shared OpenGL **Tone Mapping** shader offscreen, and writes the resulting image to disk. By default, `chaoskit-render` runs multi-threaded across available hardware threads for fast image generation, and automatically switches to deterministic single-threaded execution when a random seed (`--seed`) is supplied. Accompanying end-to-end tests invoke `chaoskit-render` on checked-in **Project** fixtures and compare the rendered images against golden reference images using a perceptual/statistical error threshold (normalized RMSE).

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want to render a binary `.ck` **Project** saved from the Qt UI into an image file from the command line, so that I can inspect or batch-render authored **Projects** without opening the interactive UI.
2. As a developer, I want to render a human-readable Protobuf text-format **Project** from the command line, so that I can author, version-control, and review compact **Project** fixtures in Git.
3. As a developer, I want the CLI to reuse the Qt implementation's **Project**-to-execution lowering (`toCameraSystem`), aspect-ratio-preserving coordinate mapping and **Histogram** accumulation (`GathererTask`), **Color Map** registry, and OpenGL 3.2 Core **Tone Mapping** shader (`GLToneMapper`), so that CLI renders match the visual output of the interactive Qt UI.
4. As a developer, I want `chaoskit-render` to run **Particle** stepping and **Histogram** gathering across all hardware threads by default without per-step lock contention, so that high-density renders complete as quickly as possible.
5. As a developer, I want to pass `--threads <N>` to explicitly control the number of worker threads during unseeded rendering, so that I can tune CPU utilization during local development or CI runs.
6. As a developer, I want passing `--seed <uint64>` to switch `chaoskit-render` into a single-threaded deterministic mode backed by a seeded PCG random number generator, so that repeated runs on the same platform produce identical **Histograms** and output images.
7. As a developer, I want `chaoskit-render` to reject combining `--seed` with `--threads` greater than 1 with a clear error message and non-zero exit code, so that I am never misled into expecting deterministic output from a multi-threaded run.
8. As a developer, I want to control the simulation budget via `--ipp <N>` / `--iterations-per-pixel <N>` (defaulting to a sensible density such as 100 plotted steps per pixel), so that rendering quality scales automatically with the **Project**'s image dimensions.
9. As a developer, I want to optionally specify an exact total count of plotted steps via `--iterations <N>` (mutually exclusive with `--ipp`), so that I can run fixed-workload renders regardless of resolution.
10. As a developer, I want each counted iteration in the CLI budget to represent one plotted **Particle** step (`process()` + `processCamera()`), so that configuring unplotted warm-up steps via minimum **Lifetime** does not starve the **Histogram** of plotted samples.
11. As a developer, I want to override the **Project**'s image `width` and `height` via `--width` and `--height` CLI flags, so that I can render thumbnails or high-resolution exports from the same **Project** file without modifying it.
12. As a developer, I want to override **Tone Mapping** parameters (`--gamma`, `--exposure`, `--vibrancy`) and the active **Color Map** (`--color-map`) via CLI flags, so that I can experiment with post-processing and color configurations from the command line.
13. As a developer, I want the CLI to apply the same fallback defaults as the Qt UI when `proto3` fields are unset/zero in a loaded **Project** (`width = 1024`, `height = 1024`, `gamma = 2.2`, and the registry's default **Color Map** when the **Color Map** name is empty), so that minimal text-format **Project** fixtures render identically to a default UI **Project**.
14. As a developer, I want all built-in **Color Maps** (`BlackWhite`, `Rainbow`, and `BGR`) to be registered in a single shared registry in the core module, so that any **Color Map** selectable in the Qt UI is also available in the CLI.
15. As a developer, I want `chaoskit-render` to fail with a non-zero exit code and descriptive error message when a non-empty **Color Map** name is not found in the registry, when the input **Project** cannot be opened or parsed, or when the output image cannot be written, so that broken configurations fail fast in scripts and tests.
16. As a developer, I want `chaoskit-render` to honor an **Isolated Blend** if present in the input **Project** (matching the Qt UI's lowering behavior) while emitting a warning to standard error, so that I can intentionally test blend isolation or immediately notice if a `.ck` file was accidentally saved with a soloed **Blend**.
17. As a developer, I want `chaoskit-render` to log any **System** lowering warnings (such as normalized **Lifetime** ranges or unrecognized **Formula** types) to standard error, so that authoring issues in **Project** fixtures are visible in CLI output.
18. As a developer, I want unhit background pixels (`point.w <= 0.0` in the **Histogram**) to evaluate to opaque black `vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)` in the OpenGL **Tone Mapping** fragment shader instead of dividing `0.0 / 0.0` (`NaN`), so that background pixels render deterministically across GPU drivers and platforms.
19. As a developer, I want an automated CTest/GTest end-to-end test suite that runs `chaoskit-render` on checked-in **Project** fixtures and compares the output against golden PNG images using normalized RMSE, so that regressions in **Formula** evaluation, **Affine Transforms**, **Camera** projection, **Coloring Methods**, **Color Maps**, **Lifetime** handling, or **Tone Mapping** are caught by `make test`.
20. As a developer, I want failed end-to-end image comparisons to write `<test>_actual.png` and `<test>_diff.png` artifacts and support an environment variable (`CHAOSKIT_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`) to regenerate golden images, so that I can easily inspect visual diffs and update reference images when intentional rendering changes are made.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Top-Level CLI Module & Executable Target**:
  - Introduce a new top-level `cli` module registered in the root CMake build, producing the `chaoskit-render` executable target and its end-to-end test target.
  - Link the CLI module against the existing `core`, `library`, `ui_core`, `ui_storage`, and `ui_colormapregistry` libraries without duplicating lowering, gathering, or shader code.
- **Shared Built-In Color Maps**:
  - Move registration of the `"BGR"` `PaletteColorMap` out of the UI application's `main()` into `core::ColorMapRegistry`'s constructor alongside `"BlackWhite"` and `"Rainbow"`, ensuring both the UI and CLI see the exact same built-in **Color Maps**.
  - Preserve `ColorMapRegistry::defaultName()`'s existing behavior (or guarantee `"BlackWhite"` is always present as fallback) when a **Project** has an empty **Color Map** name.
- **Project Loading & Normalization**:
  - Accept an input **Project** file in either binary Protobuf format or Protobuf `TextFormat` (attempting binary parse or text-format parse based on extension `.pbtxt`/`.cktxt` with fallback, rejecting files that fail both).
  - Normalize unset `proto3` zero values on the loaded `chaoskit::Project` before applying CLI overrides: if `width == 0`, set `1024`; if `height == 0`, set `1024`; if `gamma == 0.0f`, set `2.2f`. If `color_map.name` is empty, resolve to the registry's default **Color Map** name.
  - Apply any explicitly provided CLI override flags (`--width`, `--height`, `--gamma`, `--exposure`, `--vibrancy`, `--color-map`) on top of the normalized `chaoskit::Project`.
  - Lower `project.system()` via `ui::toCameraSystem()`, forwarding any emitted lowering warnings to `stderr`, and additionally emitting a warning to `stderr` if `system.has_isolated_blend()` is true.
- **CLI Argument Contract (`QCommandLineParser`)**:
  - Positional arguments: `<input-project>` and `<output-image>`.
  - Workload flags: `--ipp <N>` / `--iterations-per-pixel <N>` (default `100`) and `--iterations <N>`. Passing both `--ipp` and `--iterations` is an error (non-zero exit). Total plotted steps is `ipp * width * height` when using `--ipp`, or `iterations` when using `--iterations`.
  - Concurrency & seeding flags: `--seed <uint64>` (optional, unset by default) and `--threads <N>` (optional, defaults to `std::thread::hardware_concurrency()` with a minimum of `1` when `--seed` is unset, and `1` when `--seed` is set). Passing both `--seed` and `--threads` with a value greater than `1` is rejected with a non-zero exit code.
  - Override flags: `--width <uint>`, `--height <uint>`, `--gamma <float>`, `--exposure <float>`, `--vibrancy <float>`, `--color-map <name>`.
- **Deterministic Seeded RNG & Multi-Threaded Histogram Gathering**:
  - Introduce a deterministic `core::Rng` implementation backed by `pcg32` initialized from a explicit `uint64_t` seed for `--seed` mode, while unseeded worker threads continue to use `core::ThreadLocalRng`.
  - Add a merge/accumulation operation on `core::HistogramBuffer` (and expose access to the underlying `core::HistogramBuffer` or merge method on `ui::GathererTask`) so each worker thread can own a thread-local `ui::GathererTask` and `core::CameraSystemProcessor`, step its assigned share of plotted steps in a tight loop without `QTimer` event-loop or mutex contention, and sum the per-thread `HistogramBuffer`s into a single combined `HistogramBuffer` on completion.
- **Headless OpenGL Tone Mapping & Image Export**:
  - Guard `point.w <= 0.0` in `ui::GLToneMapper`'s fragment shader to output `vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)` early, preventing `0.0 / 0.0` (`NaN`) evaluation on unhit background pixels.
  - In `chaoskit-render`, initialize a `QGuiApplication`, create an OpenGL 3.2 Core `QSurfaceFormat`, `QOpenGLContext`, and `QOffscreenSurface`, bind a `QOpenGLFramebufferObject` of size `(width, height)`, run `ui::GLToneMapper` (`initializeGL()`, `setGamma()`, `setExposure()`, `setVibrancy()`, `syncBuffer()`, `map()`), read back the rendered `QImage` with vertical orientation matching `SystemView` in the Qt UI, and write it via `QImageWriter`.

## Testing Decisions

- **What Makes a Good Test**:
  - Tests must exercise only external behavior at the highest possible seam—never internal implementation details or private helper classes.
  - The entire feature is tested through a **single seam**: invoking the `chaoskit-render` CLI entry point (`(CLI args, input Project file) -> (exit code, stderr output, rendered output image file)`).
- **Modules Under Test**:
  - The `cli` module (`chaoskit-render`), along with its end-to-end integration across `ui_storage`, `ui_core`, `ui_colormapregistry`, `core`, and `library`.
  - Test cases at the CLI seam will cover:
    1. **End-to-end golden image verification**: Rendering representative `.pbtxt` / `.ck` **Project** fixtures (exercising multiple **Formulas**, **Affine Transforms**, **Blends**, **Camera**, **Coloring Methods**, **Color Maps**, **Lifetime** warm-up, and **Tone Mapping**) in both seeded single-threaded mode and unseeded multi-threaded mode, asserting that the normalized Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) between the rendered image and the checked-in golden PNG is within threshold.
    2. **Seeded determinism**: Verifying that two invocations with the same `--seed` produce bit-for-bit identical output images, and that different seeds produce different images.
    3. **CLI overrides & defaults**: Verifying that `--width`, `--height`, `--gamma`, `--exposure`, `--vibrancy`, `--color-map`, `--ipp`, and `--iterations` override the **Project** configuration as reflected in the output image dimensions and pixel values, and that omitted `proto3` fields fall back to UI defaults.
    4. **Error & warning handling**: Verifying non-zero exit codes for mutually exclusive flags (`--ipp` + `--iterations`, `--seed` + `--threads > 1`), unknown **Color Map** names, missing/corrupt input files, and verifying `stderr` warning output when an **Isolated Blend** is active.
- **Prior Art in the Codebase**:
  - Existing GTest suites registered via CMake `add_test` (`core_test`, `ui_storage_test`, `ui_models_test`) provide the pattern for CTest integration and Qt/GTest target configuration.

## Out of Scope

- Interactive UI changes or adding new rendering features to the Qt Quick application.
- Porting **Tone Mapping** from OpenGL GLSL to a CPU C++ implementation.
- Built-in image comparison subcommands inside the `chaoskit-render` binary itself (image comparison lives exclusively in the GTest end-to-end test target).
- Deterministic multi-threaded rendering when `--seed` is passed (passing `--seed` intentionally forces single-threaded execution).
- Wall-clock timeout stopping criteria for CLI rendering.

## Further Notes

- Architectural rationale for reusing `GLToneMapper` via an offscreen OpenGL context and per-thread `GathererTask` instances (switching to single-threaded execution on `--seed`) is recorded in ADR-0004 (*Headless CLI Rendering via Shared Offscreen OpenGL and Per-Thread Gathering*).

description:
## Parent

- `chaoskit-q6g`

## What to build

Enable fast multi-threaded **Particle** simulation and **Histogram** accumulation by default in `chaoskit-render` when `--seed` is omitted, and add workload and concurrency CLI flags (`--threads <N>`, `--ipp <N>` / `--iterations-per-pixel <N>`, and `--iterations <N>`). Worker threads step **Particles** into thread-local `GathererTask` **Histogram** buffers without lock contention and sum the buffers into a single **Histogram** before **Tone Mapping**, while passing `--seed` automatically switches execution to single-threaded deterministic mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When `--seed` is omitted, `chaoskit-render` defaults to running across `std::thread::hardware_concurrency()` worker threads (minimum 1, or `--threads <N>` when specified), each accumulating into its own thread-local `GathererTask` **Histogram** buffer merged by summation on completion.
- [ ] When `--seed` is passed, `chaoskit-render` runs on a single thread; passing both `--seed` and `--threads` greater than 1 fails with a non-zero exit code and error message.
- [ ] `--ipp <N>` / `--iterations-per-pixel <N>` (default `100`) sets the total plotted step budget to `N * width * height`, and `--iterations <N>` sets an exact total plotted step budget; passing both `--ipp` and `--iterations` fails with a non-zero exit code.
- [ ] `cli_test` verifies multi-threaded golden-image rendering (within normalized RMSE threshold), workload flag behavior (`--ipp` and `--iterations`), and error handling for invalid or conflicting `--threads`, `--seed`, `--ipp`, and `--iterations` arguments.

title: CLI Project override flags (--width, --height, --gamma, --exposure, --vibrancy, --color-map)
description:
## Parent

- `chaoskit-q6g`

## What to build

Add CLI override flags (`--width`, `--height`, `--gamma`, `--exposure`, `--vibrancy`, and `--color-map`) to `chaoskit-render` so developers can override image dimensions, **Tone Mapping** parameters, and the active **Color Map** on top of a loaded **Project** from the command line without editing the **Project** file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Passing `--width <uint>` and/or `--height <uint>` overrides the loaded **Project**'s dimensions (and scales the `--ipp` plotted-step budget and output image size accordingly); non-positive or non-numeric dimension arguments fail with a non-zero exit code.
- [ ] Passing `--gamma <float>`, `--exposure <float>`, and/or `--vibrancy <float>` overrides the loaded **Project**'s **Tone Mapping** settings before executing `GLToneMapper`; non-positive `--gamma` or malformed float values fail with a non-zero exit code.
- [ ] Passing `--color-map <name>` overrides the loaded **Project**'s **Color Map** selection, failing with a non-zero exit code if `<name>` is not registered in `ColorMapRegistry`.
- [ ] `cli_test` verifies at the CLI seam that each override flag visibly takes effect in the rendered output image and that invalid override values return a non-zero exit code.
